body.en: {entry_title} is part of a CS Unplugged unit about binary numbers. Binary is how computers store numbers using only two states, on and off. The activities use cards, movement and games, with no screen.
It is made for children about {age} and up, and it is meant to be done together with a grown-up or teacher. You do not need to know any coding. It is a {level} activity.

adult_note.en: Grown-ups: these are teacher and parent lesson plans. Be the guide, let the child discover patterns, and do not worry about correct answers at first.

steps.en: Ask a grown-up to read the lesson or open our simple version with you.
Gather what you need, like paper cards with dots, and clear a little space.
Do the activity together and say out loud what you notice.

goal.en: Do the first lesson of the unit together.

body.en: {entry_title} is part of a CS Unplugged unit about giving clear instructions to a robot, like a toy bot or a friend pretending to be one. You learn what a program is by writing one for a friend to follow.
It is for children about {age} and up who like moving around and giving or following instructions. You do not need a computer. It is a {level} activity to do with a grown-up or teacher.

adult_note.en: Grown-ups: bugs are good. Praise finding and fixing mistakes, not only getting it right the first time.

steps.en: Make a grid on the floor with tape or chalk.
Choose who is the programmer and who is the robot, and agree on simple commands.
Write the program, run it, and fix any mistakes you find.

body.en: Most lessons take 30 to 45 minutes. Plan about {minutes} minutes for a session. (estimate)

goal.en: Be the robot and follow a friend's instructions.
Write a longer program for a new route.
Add a rule and find the bugs.
Teach someone else the game.

body.en: {entry_title} is part of a CS Unplugged unit about sorting. You walk through a path drawn on the ground, comparing numbers with other people, until everyone ends up in order.
It is for children about {age} and up who like moving around and working in a team, with a grown-up or teacher. It is a {level} activity and needs chalk or tape and some space.

adult_note.en: Grown-ups: only one team walks the path at a time, so give the watchers a job, like checking the results.

steps.en: Draw the sorting path on the ground with chalk or tape.
Give six people a number each and let them walk through, comparing at each meeting.
Check if everyone ended up in order, then try new numbers.

body.en: Most lessons take 30 to 45 minutes. Plan about {minutes} minutes for a session. (estimate)

goal.en: Walk through the path with six numbers.
Try different cards, such as bigger numbers.
Sort other things, like heights.
Draw your own bigger network.
